summary: Iteration 28 — Plume Astrale Phase 1 (HeroOracle public funnel) FULLY VALIDATED. 16/16 backend pytest pass against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. POST /api/oracle/teaser is correctly PUBLIC (no auth), returns lifepath{number,archetype}, moon_phase{phase,message}, tarot{card_name,answer}, locked_preview — all under 2s (~0.5s observed). Validation behaves as spec: empty first_name -> 400, omitted field -> 422 (pydantic), invalid date format -> 400. POST /api/oracle/capture-email returns success=true even when Supabase table 'oracle_leads' does not exist (graceful try/except wrapping the upsert). Invalid email -> 400. Regression OK: /api/auth/me, /api/credits/use (chat_astral -3, karma_destin -20 verified by live balance delta), admin /api/admin/users/{id}/credits (delta=+5) and /api/admin/users/{id}/premium (grant_days then revoke, both 200).
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by test agent: GET /api/health was missing — only @app.get('/health') existed and the spec explicitly required /api/health. Added @app.get('/api/health') in server.py mirroring the existing handler. Note: declaring @api_router.get('/health') AFTER app.include_router(api_router) would NOT register the route (FastAPI freezes the router tree at include time) — so the route was attached directly to `app`. Main agent may want to relocate it to be next to api_router include for cleanliness.

routes/oracle.py: chemin_de_vie fallback (lines 142-146) catches a broad Exception and reduces by digit-sum which silently strips master numbers 11/22/33. Today's test (1976-11-22 -> 11) works because _chemin_de_vie_iso succeeded, but if it ever raises the fallback drops the master. Suggest using numerology_service.reduce_with_masters() instead.

routes/oracle.py:_moon_phase_simple ignores the `date_str` argument it receives — phase is computed only from datetime.now(). Currently OK per spec ('phase lunaire du jour'), but variable name is misleading. Consider renaming param to `_unused` or computing from birth_date if product later wants natal moon phase.

routes/oracle.py:_tarot_oui_non uses Python hash() which is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED). Result therefore changes after every backend restart for the same (first_name, birth_date, today) triplet — Phase 1 spec implies determinism within the day. Use hashlib.sha256 for a stable seed.

routes/oracle.py:capture-email swallows ALL exceptions silently (line 189). For observability, switch the print to logger.warning and include the supabase error code; otherwise oracle_leads insert failures will be invisible in prod.
Pydantic v2: EmailCaptureRequest.email is typed `str`. Switching to `EmailStr` (already a transitive dep via pydantic[email]) would give cleaner 422s without hand-rolled '@ in email' check.

server.py is 1182 lines — exceeds the 700-line code-review threshold. Recommend splitting tarot/numerology/horoscope/payments into their own route modules (matching the pattern already established by routes/oracle.py, routes/astrology_v3.py, routes/admin.py).
seed_data_creation: None. capture-email test data uses prefix TEST_ but Supabase oracle_leads insert is best-effort (will simply log warning if table is absent).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 1 acquisition funnel is wired correctly. The /api/oracle/teaser endpoint is fully deterministic-per-day (modulo PYTHONHASHSEED — see code review) and PUBLIC. capture-email gracefully handles a missing oracle_leads table. /api/health endpoint was added during this iteration. No retest required. If product wants stable card-of-the-day across restarts, swap hash() for hashlib.sha256 in routes/oracle.py:_tarot_oui_non.
rca of the issue: Single deviation from spec — /api/health 404 — was caused by the health route being declared on `app` instead of `api_router`. Fixed in-place by adding a second handler at /api/health directly on `app`.
